summary: Tsyben Zhamtsarano (1880–1942) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902 and later headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

Tu Weiming (born 1940) specializes in philosophy, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Tunghai University and Harvard, taught at Princeton, UC Berkeley, and Harvard, and later directed Peking University's Institute for Advanced Humanistic Studies.

Tubten Chokyi Dorje studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught numerous students, including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Tubten Gyeltsen Ozer was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Tubten Nyendrak (1883–1959) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Dodrupchen Rinpoche and Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima.
Tubten Nyima was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Tsondru studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Khenpo Gangshar. His own students included Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche and Ringu Tulku.

Tukaram Ramchandra Laddu was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg by 1912 and held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1920.
Tulku Hungkar Dorje is a scholar who studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Tulku Sherdor (born 1961) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia under Ted Norton and Jeffrey Hopkins, and trained traditionally under Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

Tulku Thondup (1939–2023) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dodrupchen Monastery under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche (1920–1996) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Samten Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and others, founded Tergar Osel Ling Monastery, and taught numerous prominent students.

Turrell V. Wylie (1927–1984) worked in Tibetology, linguistics, and sinology. He studied at the University of Washington and under Giuseppe Tucci and Dezhung Rinpoche, later serving as Professor of Tibetan Language and Civilization at Washington.
Tutob Chökyi Wangchuk was a scholar who studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Trulshik Rinpoche.
Tyler Dewar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Nitartha Institute and under traditional teachers Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, and Tashi Wangchuk.

Tzungkuen Wen specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Queensland and held posts at Fuyan Buddhist Institute in 2005 and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, attested for 2026.
Ugyen Pelgen works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned a master's degree from Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

Ulrich Pagel specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme, and held a post at SOAS University of London attested between 2013 and 2020.

Ulrich Timme Kragh (born 1969) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and held posts at Copenhagen, Geumgang University, IIAS, and the University of Sydney.

Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff (1848–1931) worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Bonn and Berlin, and held professorships at the University of Greifswald, University of Göttingen, and Frederick William University Berlin.
